text:
Incident Bot: Paging oncall: possible TLS handshake failures across hosted-api in us-east-1 (alerts spiking)

Alex G.: i’m getting paged — looking at the alert graphs now. spikes at 11:03 UTC.

Priya S.: oncall here, i'm in. first pass: 504s and a bunch of 525 TLS errors in our client-facing LB logs. customers seeing transient 5xx.

Mike R.: saw an automation alert: cert-rotation job for hosted-api completed ~10:58 UTC. Ops runbook shows rotation then rollout to gateway fleet.

Lia T.: i can tail the gateway logs, grabbing the handshake failures.

Eva C.: adding timeline in-thread:
- 10:57 UTC: deployment window, cert rotation job started
- 10:58 UTC: cert rotation job reports success and pushed to s3://redwood-certs/stage
- 11:01 UTC: first Grafana alert for increased 525s
- 11:03 UTC: incident-bot page

NetOps: we also accepted a VPC peering route change earlier today for edge-pop testing, last change at 09:50 UTC. worth checking.

Priya S.: ok hypotheses: (1) faulty cert chain/rotation produced invalid certs, (2) new cert chain increases TLS record sizes and combined with MTU/peering causes handshake issues, (3) gateway bug in cert hot reload.

Alex G.: Lia, can you paste sample gateway error logs (redact IPs) and tcpdump from failed handshake?

Lia T.: paste snippets below:

```
[2026-03-14T11:03:12Z] WARN tls: handshake error from 10.0.5.23: remote error: tls: handshake failure
[2026-03-14T11:03:12Z] DEBUG tls: certificate chain length = 4, total size = 3784 bytes
[2026-03-14T11:03:12Z] ERROR proxy: upstream connection failed: write tcp: write: connection reset by peer
```

And tcpdump of the server side showing retransmits and ICMP frag needed not being delivered:

```
11:03:12.345678 IP client > gw: Flags [P.], seq 1:1481, ack 1, win 64240, length 1480
11:03:12.346000 IP gw > client: Flags [.], ack 1481, win 63712, length 0
11:03:12.346200 IP client > gw: Flags [P.], seq 1481:2961, ack 1, length 1480
11:03:12.346400 IP gw > router: ICMP frag needed and DF set, mtu 1400
11:03:12.346600 IP router > client: ICMP forbidden (filtered)
11:03:12.347000 TCP gw > client: RST, seq 0
```

Priya S.: that ICMP line is interesting — suggests PMTU blackhole. if ICMP messages are being blocked somewhere along the peering path, big TLS records could get dropped and handshake stalls.

Mike R.: remember we increased cert chain length (added two intermediate certs) to support new CA. that increases initial record sizes.

NetOps: checking peering ACLs and route tables now. i see the new peering had jumbo frames enabled on one side (MTU 9000) but transit devices expect 1500. that can create fragmentation mismatches.

Eva C.: so combined scenario: cert rotation -> larger TLS records -> VPC peering MTU mismatch + blocked ICMP -> PMTU discovery fails -> large records dropped -> handshake fails. seems plausible.

Priya S.: mitigation options: 1) roll back cert rotation to previous certs (fast but loses new ca), 2) enforce TCP MSS clamp on peering to 1400, 3) temporarily disable DF or adjust MTU on hosts, 4) adjust peering ACLs to permit ICMP type 3 code 4.

Alex G.: do we have customer-impacted list? any SLO breaches?

Eva C.: early check: ~3% of requests to hosted-api returned 5xx between 11:01-11:10 UTC. a few enterprise customers saw higher error rates. Logged a support ticket to notify top 10 customers.

Lia T.: attempting TCP MSS clamp on gateway host (non-prod first):

```
# sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
# iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

Priya S.: good. while lia tests that in a canary pool, mike pls prepare rollback of cert rotation (clear rollout tags). Lia, if MSS clamp fixes handshake in canary we'll apply cluster-wide.

NetOps: ACL change to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 is in progress. pushing policy change to peering devices now. ETA ~8 min.

Incident Bot: Ops runbook reminder: during network degradation >5% errors, declare P1 if customer-impacting. Current classification: P2; evaluating escalation.

Alex G.: we should escalate to P1 if top customers are affected. Eva, coordinate customer comms.

Eva C.: drafting status update to affected customers now. linking to internal status page.

~8 minutes pass~

Lia T.: canary results: after applying MSS clamp to 2 gateways, handshake success rate went from 86% -> 99% for that pool.

Mike R.: rolling MSS clamp to remaining gateways now (rolling, 2 at a time). also initiating cert rollback to previous chain as conservative measure.

Priya S.: monitoring metrics — error rate dropping. will keep watch for 30m.

NetOps: ACL change completed. confirmed ICMP frag messages now reach origin.

Alex G.: good. mitigation: MSS clamp deployed cluster-wide and peering ACL fixed. cert rollback completed. impact window: 11:01-11:18 UTC.

Eva C.: preparing incident summary for customers and internal post-incident. note: avoid long cert chains until peering MTU is validated.

Mike R.: quick logs that led to final hypothesis (from gateway after MSS clamp):

```
[2026-03-14T11:09:45Z] INFO tls: handshake completed for conn_id=abc123, chain_size=1750 bytes
[2026-03-14T11:08:59Z] WARN tls: previous handshake failed: write: connection reset by peer (likely path MTU)
```

Priya S.: next actions / RCA tasks (tracking here):
- [ ] NetOps to document peering MTU config and remove jumbo frames mismatch (NetOps)
- [ ] Infra to add tcp_mss clamp as a default on gateway ASG (Mike R.)
- [ ] Release to add preflight check in cert rollout to estimate chain size and simulate handshake over low MTU (Lia T.)
- [ ] SRE to add alert rule: sudden increase in TLS record size + PMTU ICMP drops (Priya S.)
- [ ] Support to follow up with impacted customers (Eva C.)

Alex G.: noted. also add runbook step: when cert rotation touches gateway fleet, check path MTU and allow ICMP for that window. Ops Runbook Bot, please create followup checklist.

Ops Runbook Bot: Created followup checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incidents/2533333333-followup

Priya S.: tagging final timeline for RCA doc. will start draft and assign owners.

Eva C.: customer update posted at 11:40 UTC: short outage window explained, mitigation steps, points of contact.

Alex G.: closing incident channel in 30m if all stable. thanks everyone for quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

NetOps: FYI — root cause summary for RCA: MTU mismatch on new VPC peering + increased TLS record sizes from new cert chain; ICMP filtering caused PMTU discovery failure; led to TCP resets and handshake failures. Remediation: enforce MSS clamp, normalize MTU configs, preflight cert rollouts, update runbooks, improve monitoring.

Priya S.: marking this thread as incident timeline + in-incident RCA coordination. final message timestamped here.

Incident Bot: Incident resolved (P2 -> resolved). Incident channel will be archived after the postmortem is published.
